rules.rule_name: Detect Missing Active Session on Delete User Screen Access
rules.rule_description: When a user attempts to access the Delete User screen, the system must verify that an active session exists (communication area is present). If no active session is found, the user must be redirected away from the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is There an Active Session?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Delete User screen
acceptance_criteria.When: No active session communication area exists (session length equals zero)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system determines that no active session is present and initiates a redirect to the Sign-On screen

rules.rule_name: Set Sign-On Screen as Redirect Destination for Unauthenticated Access
rules.rule_description: When no active session is detected, the system must designate the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) as the target destination before performing the redirect.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Destination to Sign-On Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Delete User screen and no active session exists
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines the session is missing
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On screen identified as COSGN00C

rules.rule_name: Record Current Program and Transaction Details Before Redirect
rules.rule_description: Before redirecting an unauthenticated user to the Sign-On screen, the system must record the current transaction ID and program name into the communication area so that navigation context is preserved.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Program and Transaction Details

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that no active session exists and the destination has been set to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control away from the Delete User screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction ID into the communication area field for the originating transaction, records the current program name into the communication area field for the originating program, and resets the program context indicator to zero

rules.rule_name: Redirect Unauthenticated User to Sign-On Screen
rules.rule_description: After recording navigation context, the system must transfer control to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C), passing the communication area so that session state is maintained for the sign-on process.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redirect User to Sign-On Screen COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: No active session exists, the destination has been set to COSGN00C, and the current program and transaction details have been recorded in the communication area
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the redirect
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the Sign-On screen program COSGN00C, passing the full communication area so that the sign-on screen has access to the navigation context

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the User Deletion screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No active session communication area exists (session length equals zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) and transfers control to it, ending the current program execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redirect Unauthenticated Session to Sign-On Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no active session exists upon program entry, the user is redirected to the Sign-On screen to authenticate before accessing the User Deletion function.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An active session exists and the User Deletion screen is being accessed for the first time (program re-entry flag is not set)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen initializes for first-time display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the screen as re-enterable, clears all screen output fields to low-values, sets the cursor on the User ID input field, and if a User ID was pre-selected from the previous screen (not spaces or low-values), pre-populates the User ID field with that value and automatically performs a user lookup before displaying the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize User Deletion Screen on First Access
all_rules.Rule_Description: On the first access to the User Deletion screen within an active session, the screen is initialized and, if a user was pre-selected from a prior screen, their User ID is automatically populated and a lookup is performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Deletion screen is displayed and the user has pressed the ENTER key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID input field contains only spaces or low-values (is empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the User ID field, and redisplays the User Deletion screen without performing any lookup

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate User ID is Not Empty on ENTER Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the ENTER key to look up a user, the User ID field must contain a value. An empty User ID is not permitted to proceed with the lookup.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Deletion screen is displayed, the user has pressed ENTER, and the User ID field contains a non-empty value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system searches the User Security File (USRSEC) using the entered User ID as the key, acquiring an update lock on the record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the user record is found, the system retrieves the user's First Name, Last Name, and User Type from the security file and proceeds to display those details on screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Look Up User Details from Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid non-empty User ID is entered and ENTER is pressed, the system retrieves the user's details from the User Security File to display for confirmation prior to deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a User ID and pressed ENTER to perform a lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security File (USRSEC) does not contain a record matching the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'User ID NOT found...', positions the cursor on the User ID field, and redisplays the User Deletion screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User Not Found Error During Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered User ID does not exist in the User Security File during a lookup, the system informs the user that the record was not found.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a User ID and pressed ENTER, and the User Security File (USRSEC) has returned a matching record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user record is successfully retrieved from the security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the screen with the user's First Name, Last Name, and User Type from the security file, displays the informational message 'Press PF5 key to delete this user...', sets the message color to neutral, and redisplays the User Deletion screen awaiting PF5 confirmation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User Details and Prompt for Deletion Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a user record is successfully found in the security file, the system displays the user's details and prompts the operator to confirm deletion by pressing PF5, implementing a two-step deletion confirmation process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Deletion screen is displayed with user details and the user has pressed PF5 to confirm deletion
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID field contains a non-empty value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system re-reads the user record from the User Security File (USRSEC) with an update lock using the User ID as the key, and if the record is found, proceeds to execute the deletion of that user record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initiate User Record Deletion on PF5 Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF5 to confirm deletion, the system validates the User ID is present, re-reads the user record from the security file, and proceeds to delete it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF5 to initiate deletion of a user record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID input field contains only spaces or low-values (is empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...', positions the cursor on the User ID field, and redisplays the User Deletion screen without performing any deletion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate User ID is Not Empty Before Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before executing a user deletion, the system enforces that the User ID field is not empty to prevent unintended or invalid deletion attempts.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to delete a user record from the User Security File (USRSEC) after PF5 was pressed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The deletion operation completes successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears all screen input fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type) and the message area, sets the message color to green, constructs and displays the confirmation message 'User [User ID] has been deleted...' where [User ID] is the deleted user's ID, and redisplays the User Deletion screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm Successful User Deletion with Green Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful deletion of a user record from the security file, the system clears all input fields and displays a green-colored confirmation message identifying the deleted user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Deletion screen is displayed with data in one or more fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF4 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears all input fields including User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type, and the message area, sets the cursor length on the User ID field to -1, and redisplays the blank User Deletion screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Screen Fields on PF4 Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF4, all input fields on the User Deletion screen are cleared, allowing the user to start a new search or deletion from a clean state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Deletion screen is displayed and the user has pressed the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: PF3 is pressed to navigate back
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) is recorded and not spaces or low-values, the system transfers control to that originating program; otherwise, the system transfers control to the Administration Menu (COADM01C), passing the current transaction ID, program name, and communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate Back to Previous Screen on PF3 Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3, the system returns control to the screen from which the User Deletion screen was originally invoked, defaulting to the Administration Menu if no originating screen is recorded.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Deletion screen is displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF12 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Administration Menu (COADM01C) and transfers control to it, passing the current transaction ID, program name, and communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate Directly to Administration Menu on PF12 Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF12, the system unconditionally transfers control to the Administration Menu, regardless of the navigation history.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Deletion screen is displayed and awaiting user input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key other than ENTER, PF3, PF4, PF5, or PF12
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', populates the message area with the standard invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY), and redisplays the User Deletion screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Invalid Key Press with Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses any key other than the supported function keys (ENTER, PF3, PF4, PF5, PF12), the system displays an invalid key error message and redisplays the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Deletion screen is about to be sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population routine is executed prior to any screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time, formats the date as MM-DD-YY and the time as HH-MM-SS, and populates the screen header fields with: Application Title 1 (CCDA-TITLE01), Application Title 2 (CCDA-TITLE02), current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID), current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME), formatted current date, and formatted current time

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Header with Current Date, Time, and Program Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every time the User Deletion screen is displayed, the header section is refreshed with the application titles, current program name, transaction ID, and the current system date and time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user deletion screen is being accessed for the first time (the screen has not yet been marked as re-enterable)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initializes the user deletion screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All screen output display fields are cleared (set to low-values), the cursor is positioned on the User ID input field, and the screen is marked as re-enterable to handle subsequent interactions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize User Deletion Screen on First Access
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user deletion screen is accessed for the first time in a session, all screen display fields must be cleared and the cursor must be positioned on the User ID input field to prepare for fresh user input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user deletion screen is being initialized for the first time
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks the pre-selected User ID value passed from the previous screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the pre-selected User ID is not empty (not spaces and not low-values), the system proceeds to pre-populate the User ID field and perform an automatic user lookup; otherwise, the system displays an empty user deletion screen ready for manual input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Pre-Selected User ID from Previous Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: During screen initialization, the system must check whether a User ID was already selected and passed from a previous screen in the navigation flow, to determine whether to auto-populate and look up the user or display a blank screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user deletion screen is being initialized for the first time AND a valid User ID (non-blank, non-empty) was passed from the previous screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system pre-populates the screen fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID input field on the deletion screen is populated with the User ID value that was selected and passed from the previous screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Pre-Populate User ID Field with Previously Selected User
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a User ID has been passed from a previous screen, the system must automatically populate the User ID input field on the deletion screen with that pre-selected value, eliminating the need for the user to manually re-enter the ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user deletion screen is being initialized for the first time AND the User ID field has been pre-populated with a value passed from the previous screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system automatically initiates the user lookup process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system searches the User Security File using the pre-populated User ID as the search key; if the user is found, the user details are retrieved and a message 'Press PF5 key to delete this user ...' is prepared; if the User ID is not found in the security file, an error message 'User ID NOT found...' is displayed and the cursor is placed on the User ID field; if the lookup cannot be completed due to a system issue, an error message 'Unable to lookup User...' is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Automatic User Lookup for Pre-Selected User ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a User ID has been pre-populated from a previous screen selection, the system must automatically trigger a user lookup against the security file to retrieve the user's details without requiring the user to press ENTER manually.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user lookup against the User Security File was successful and the user record was found
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the deletion screen with the retrieved user information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen displays the user's First Name (from the security file), Last Name (from the security file), and User Type (from the security file) in their respective fields, along with the message 'Press PF5 key to delete this user ...' to prompt the administrator for the next action, and the screen is rendered with the current date, current time, transaction name, and program name in the header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Retrieved User Details on Deletion Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful user lookup, the system must display the retrieved user's personal details on the deletion screen so the administrator can verify the correct user before confirming deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user deletion screen is being initialized for the first time AND no User ID was passed from the previous screen (the pre-selected User ID is blank or empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system renders the user deletion screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An empty user deletion screen is displayed with all input fields blank (User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type), the cursor positioned on the User ID field, no error messages shown, and the screen header populated with the current date, current time, transaction name, and program name

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Empty User Deletion Screen When No User Pre-Selected
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no User ID has been pre-selected from a previous screen, the system must display a blank user deletion screen, allowing the administrator to manually enter the User ID of the user they wish to delete.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Delete screen is displayed and the user has pressed the Enter key to look up a user record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID input field is empty (contains spaces or no value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to ON, (2) display the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...' in the screen message area, (3) position the cursor on the User ID input field, and (4) redisplay the User Delete screen — preventing any user lookup from being performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate User ID is Not Empty on Enter Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the Enter key to look up a user, the system must validate that the User ID field contains a value. If the User ID field is blank, the system sets an error condition, displays an error message, and prompts the user to provide a valid User ID before proceeding.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Delete screen is displayed and the user has pressed the Enter key to look up a user record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID input field contains a non-blank value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) position the cursor on the User ID field, (2) clear the First Name, Last Name, and User Type fields on the screen, (3) copy the entered User ID as the search key, and (4) proceed to look up the user record in the security file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Allow User Lookup to Proceed When User ID is Provided on Enter Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the Enter key and the User ID field contains a value, the system clears any prior user detail fields and proceeds to look up the user record from the security file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Delete screen is displayed and the user has pressed the PF5 key to delete a user record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID input field is empty (contains spaces or no value)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) set the error flag to ON, (2) display the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...' in the screen message area, (3) position the cursor on the User ID input field, and (4) redisplay the User Delete screen — preventing any deletion from being performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate User ID is Not Empty on PF5 Delete Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the PF5 key to delete a user, the system must validate that the User ID field contains a value. If the User ID field is blank, the system sets an error condition, displays an error message, and prompts the user to provide a valid User ID before any deletion is attempted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Delete screen is displayed and the user has pressed the PF5 key to delete a user record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID input field contains a non-blank value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) position the cursor on the User ID field, (2) copy the entered User ID as the search key, (3) proceed to read the user record from the security file, and (4) if the read is successful, proceed to execute the deletion of the user record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Allow Delete to Proceed When User ID is Provided on PF5 Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the PF5 key to delete a user and the User ID field contains a value, the system proceeds to look up the user record in the security file as a prerequisite before executing the deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a User ID on the User Deletion screen and pressed ENTER to initiate a lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins processing the lookup request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears the First Name, Last Name, and User Type fields on the screen before performing the search, ensuring no previously displayed user data remains visible

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Screen Fields Before User Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before performing a user lookup, the system clears the First Name, Last Name, and User Type fields on the User Deletion screen to ensure no stale data is displayed during the search.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User ID field on the User Deletion screen contains a non-blank value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to search the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system uses the entered User ID as the unique identifier (search key) to locate the user record in the User Security file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set User ID as Search Key for Security File Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: The User ID entered on the screen is used as the unique search key to locate the corresponding user record in the User Security file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid non-blank User ID has been entered on the User Deletion screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system searches the User Security file using the User ID as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system attempts to locate and retrieve the user record from the User Security file, locking the record for a potential update or deletion operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Search User Security File for User Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system searches the User Security file (USRSEC) using the provided User ID to retrieve the user's profile information. The record is retrieved with an update lock to support a potential subsequent deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched the User Security file using the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A matching user record is found in the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the user's First Name, Last Name, and User Type from the security file and populates those fields on the User Deletion screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve and Display User Details on Successful Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user record is successfully found in the User Security file, the system retrieves the user's First Name, Last Name, and User Type and populates the corresponding fields on the User Deletion screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully found and retrieved the user record from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user details are being prepared for display on the User Deletion screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the screen message to 'Press PF5 key to delete this user...' to prompt the operator to explicitly confirm the deletion action by pressing PF5

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Deletion Confirmation Prompt After Successful User Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving a user's details from the User Security file, the system displays a prompt message instructing the user to press PF5 to proceed with the deletion. This enforces a two-step confirmation process before any deletion occurs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user's First Name, Last Name, and User Type have been successfully retrieved from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the User Deletion screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the First Name field with the user's first name, the Last Name field with the user's last name, and the User Type field with the user's type on the User Deletion screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate User Deletion Screen with Retrieved User Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system populates the User Deletion screen with the retrieved user's First Name, Last Name, and User Type so the operator can review the user's information before confirming deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Deletion screen has been populated with the retrieved user's First Name, Last Name, User Type, and the prompt message 'Press PF5 key to delete this user...'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the updated screen to the operator
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the User Deletion screen with the user's details, the confirmation prompt message, and a refreshed header containing the current date, current time, transaction name, and program name

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User Deletion Screen with User Details and Confirmation Prompt
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving and populating user details, the system refreshes and displays the User Deletion screen showing the user's information along with the deletion confirmation prompt, current date, time, transaction name, and program name in the header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched the User Security file using the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No matching user record is found in the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to indicate an error condition, displays the error message 'User ID NOT found...' on the screen, and positions the cursor on the User ID field so the operator can enter a different User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Error When User ID Not Found in Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered User ID does not exist in the User Security file, the system displays an error message and repositions the cursor to the User ID field, prompting the operator to enter a valid User ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A User ID has been entered on the User Delete screen and submitted for lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system searches the User Security File using the entered User ID as the unique search key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system attempts to retrieve the user record matching the provided User ID from the User Security File, and the result determines whether the user exists or not

all_rules.Rule_Name: Search User ID in User Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user submits a User ID for lookup, the system searches the User Security File using the entered User ID as the search key to retrieve the corresponding user record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A User ID has been submitted for lookup and the system has searched the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No matching user record is found in the User Security File for the entered User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the Error Flag to ON ('Y'), which blocks any further processing steps such as displaying user details or executing a deletion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Error Flag When User ID Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User Security File search returns no matching record for the entered User ID, the system activates the error flag to indicate a failed lookup, preventing any further processing such as displaying user details or proceeding with deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched the User Security File and the Error Flag has been set to ON due to no matching record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID entered does not exist in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the screen error message to 'User ID NOT found...' to notify the user that the entered User ID does not exist

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User Not Found Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User Security File search finds no matching record for the entered User ID, the system sets a specific error message to inform the user that the entered User ID does not exist in the system.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined that the entered User ID does not exist in the User Security File and the error message 'User ID NOT found...' has been set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is being prepared for redisplay after the not-found error
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system positions the cursor to the User ID input field (USRIDINL set to -1) so the user can immediately correct or re-enter a valid User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reposition Cursor to User ID Field After Not Found Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a User Not Found error is detected, the system repositions the screen cursor back to the User ID input field, guiding the user to correct the invalid User ID entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Error Flag is ON, the error message is set to 'User ID NOT found...', and the cursor is positioned on the User ID field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the User Delete screen after a not-found error
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system refreshes the screen header with the current date, current time, transaction name, and program name, displays the error message 'User ID NOT found...' on the screen, and renders the User Delete screen with the cursor placed on the User ID field so the user can enter a different User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay Screen with User Not Found Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: After setting the error flag, error message, and cursor position due to a User Not Found condition, the system redisplays the User Delete screen showing the error message, allowing the user to enter a different User ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An administrator has entered a valid User ID on the User Deletion screen and submitted it for lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system searches the User Security File using the entered User ID as the key and the user record is found successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the complete user record containing User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type from the User Security File and makes it available for display on the confirmation screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve User Record from Security File for Deletion Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a User ID is entered and the system successfully locates the user in the security file, the full user record (including First Name, Last Name, and User Type) is retrieved and held for display on the deletion confirmation screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security File with no errors
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the User Deletion confirmation screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the screen with: First Name field set to the retrieved user's First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME), Last Name field set to the retrieved user's Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME), and User Type field set to the retrieved user's User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Fields with Retrieved User Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully retrieving a user record from the security file, the system populates the deletion confirmation screen fields with the user's First Name, Last Name, and User Type so the administrator can verify the correct user before confirming deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security File and no errors have occurred during the lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the User Deletion confirmation screen fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The First Name field on the screen is set to the First Name value (SEC-USR-FNAME) from the retrieved user security record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set First Name on Deletion Confirmation Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The user's First Name retrieved from the security file is placed into the First Name display field on the User Deletion screen to allow the administrator to visually confirm the correct user's identity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security File and no errors have occurred during the lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the User Deletion confirmation screen fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Last Name field on the screen is set to the Last Name value (SEC-USR-LNAME) from the retrieved user security record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Last Name on Deletion Confirmation Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The user's Last Name retrieved from the security file is placed into the Last Name display field on the User Deletion screen to allow the administrator to visually confirm the correct user's identity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security File and no errors have occurred during the lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the User Deletion confirmation screen fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User Type field on the screen is set to the User Type value (SEC-USR-TYPE) from the retrieved user security record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set User Type on Deletion Confirmation Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The user's User Type retrieved from the security file is placed into the User Type display field on the User Deletion screen to allow the administrator to visually confirm the correct user's role before deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The administrator has entered a User ID and the system has successfully located the user record in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the User Deletion screen for display after a successful user lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the screen message to 'Press PF5 key to delete this user ...' displayed in neutral color, indicating to the administrator that an explicit PF5 key press is required to confirm and execute the deletion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Deletion Confirmation Prompt Message After Successful User Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a user is successfully found in the security file, the system displays a specific instructional prompt message guiding the administrator to press PF5 to proceed with deletion. This enforces a mandatory two-step confirmation process before any user is deleted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the User Deletion screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population routine is executed prior to sending the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the screen header with: Application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01), Application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02), Transaction Name (WS-TRANID), Program Name (WS-PGMNAME), Current Date formatted as MM-DD-YY derived from the system's current date, and Current Time formatted as HH-MM-SS derived from the system's current time

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Header with Current Application and Session Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every time the User Deletion screen is displayed, the screen header is refreshed with the current application titles, program name, transaction identifier, and the current system date and time to provide accurate context to the administrator.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen fields have been populated with the retrieved user's First Name, Last Name, and User Type, the confirmation prompt message 'Press PF5 key to delete this user ...' has been set, and the screen header has been populated with current date, time, transaction ID, and program name
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the User Deletion screen (Map COUSR3A from Mapset COUSR03) to the administrator's terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is displayed showing: the User ID as entered by the administrator, the retrieved First Name, Last Name, and User Type of the user, the confirmation prompt message in the message area, the current application title, program name, transaction ID, current date, and current time in the header — with the cursor positioned and the screen fully refreshed (erased and rewritten)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User Deletion Confirmation Screen with All User Details and Prompt
all_rules.Rule_Description: The User Deletion screen is sent to the administrator displaying all retrieved user information along with the confirmation prompt message, enabling the administrator to review the user details and decide whether to proceed with deletion or cancel.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Deletion confirmation screen has been displayed with the user's details (User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type) and the prompt 'Press PF5 key to delete this user ...'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system returns control to the administrator awaiting a response
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system holds the current state and waits for the administrator to press one of the following keys: PF5 to confirm and execute the deletion, PF3 to return to the previous screen, PF4 to clear the screen, PF12 to return to the Administration Menu, or ENTER to perform another user lookup — and no deletion action is taken until PF5 is explicitly pressed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Await Administrator Action After Displaying User Details for Deletion Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After displaying the user details and confirmation prompt, the system returns control to the administrator and waits for an explicit action. The administrator must actively choose to confirm deletion (PF5), cancel and return to the previous screen (PF3 or PF12), clear the screen (PF4), or perform another lookup (ENTER). No deletion occurs without an explicit PF5 key press.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Delete User screen is displayed and the user has pressed PF5 to initiate a deletion
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID input field is blank or contains only spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...', place the cursor on the User ID field, and redisplay the Delete User screen without performing any lookup or deletion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate User ID is Not Empty Before Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user attempts to delete a user record by pressing PF5, the system must validate that the User ID field contains a value before proceeding with any lookup or deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Delete User screen is displayed, the user has pressed PF5, and the User ID field contains a non-blank value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the deletion process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must search the User Security File using the entered User ID to confirm the user record exists before proceeding with deletion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Look Up User in Security File Before Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before permanently deleting a user, the system must verify the user exists in the User Security File by performing a lookup using the entered User ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF5 with a non-blank User ID and the system has searched the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID is not found in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the error message 'User ID NOT found...', place the cursor on the User ID field, and redisplay the Delete User screen without performing any deletion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle User Not Found During Pre-Deletion Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the entered User ID does not exist in the User Security File during the pre-deletion lookup, the system must inform the user and prevent deletion from proceeding.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF5, the User ID is non-blank, and the user record has been found and locked in the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the deletion of the user record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The user record must be permanently and irreversibly removed from the User Security File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Permanently Delete User Record from Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the user record is confirmed to exist in the User Security File, the system permanently removes the user record from the system.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to permanently delete the user record from the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The deletion operation fails because the user record is not found
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the error message 'User ID NOT found...', place the cursor on the User ID field, and redisplay the Delete User screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Deletion Failure - User Record Not Found at Delete Step
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the deletion operation fails because the user record is no longer found at the time of deletion, the system must notify the user with an appropriate error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully and permanently deleted the user record from the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The deletion operation completes successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must clear all screen fields including User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type; display a green-colored success message in the format 'User [User ID] has been deleted...'; and redisplay the Delete User screen to confirm the deletion is complete

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Screen Fields and Display Success Confirmation After Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful deletion of a user record, the system must clear all input fields on the screen and display a green-colored confirmation message identifying the deleted user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Delete User screen is active and the user presses PF5 to delete a user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The deletion process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must strictly follow the sequence: (1) validate User ID is not empty, (2) search and lock the user record in the User Security File, and (3) only if the record is found and locked, proceed to permanently delete it — skipping deletion entirely if any prior step fails

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enforce Sequential Lookup-Then-Delete Process for User Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: The user deletion process must follow a strict sequence: validate User ID, look up the user record, and only then perform deletion. Deletion cannot occur without a prior successful lookup confirming the user exists.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully deleted from the security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the deletion was completed without errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must clear all screen input fields: User ID field is set to spaces, First Name field is set to spaces, Last Name field is set to spaces, User Type field is set to spaces, and the cursor length indicator for User ID is reset to -1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Screen Fields Upon Successful User Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a user record has been successfully deleted from the security file, all input fields on the User Deletion screen must be cleared to reset the screen to a clean state, preventing any residual data from being displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully deleted from the security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is preparing to display the deletion confirmation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must clear the working storage message field (WS-MESSAGE) by setting it to spaces before constructing the new success message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Existing Message Area After Successful Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a user record has been successfully deleted, any previously displayed message in the message area must be cleared before the new success message is built and displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully deleted from the security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is preparing the confirmation message for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the error message color attribute on the screen (ERRMSGC of COUSR3AO) to GREEN, so the success message is rendered in green color

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Success Message Color to Green for Deletion Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: To visually distinguish a successful deletion from error conditions, the message displayed after a successful user deletion must appear in green color on the screen, providing a clear positive visual indicator to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully deleted from the security file and the message area has been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system constructs the deletion confirmation message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must build the message by concatenating: the literal text 'User ', followed by the deleted User ID (SEC-USR-ID, trimmed of trailing spaces), followed by the literal text ' has been deleted ...', and store the resulting string in the message field (WS-MESSAGE) for display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build Deletion Success Message Including the Deleted User ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful deletion, the system must construct a confirmation message that explicitly identifies which user was deleted, by combining the static text 'User', the deleted User ID, and the static text 'has been deleted...' into a single message string.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the User Deletion screen after a successful deletion
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population routine (POPULATE-HEADER-INFO) is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must populate the screen header with: Application Title 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) in TITLE01O, Application Title 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) in TITLE02O, the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) in TRNNAMEO, the current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME) in PGMNAMEO, the current system date formatted as MM-DD-YY in CURDATEO, and the current system time formatted as HH-MM-SS in CURTIMEO

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Header with Current Session Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every time the User Deletion screen is displayed, the screen header must be refreshed with the current application titles, program name, transaction ID, and the current system date and time to ensure accurate session context is always shown to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All screen fields have been cleared, the success message has been built with the deleted User ID, the message color has been set to green, and the screen header has been populated with current session information
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the User Deletion screen (SEND-USRDEL-SCREEN) after a successful deletion
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the User Deletion screen (map COUSR3A from mapset COUSR03) with: all input fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type) shown as empty, the success message 'User [UserID] has been deleted ...' displayed in green color in the message area, the screen fully refreshed (ERASE), and the cursor positioned appropriately — then await the next user action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User Deletion Screen with Green Success Message and Cleared Fields
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful user deletion, the system must send the User Deletion screen to the user showing all input fields cleared and the green-colored success message confirming which user was deleted, then await the next user action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Deletion screen is active and displayed to the user, and the user is on a re-entry (the screen has already been presented once)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF4 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system invokes the Clear Current Screen process, which clears all input fields and resets the screen to its initial empty state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Screen Clear on PF4 Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the PF4 key on the User Deletion screen, the system initiates the screen clearing process by invoking the clear screen function.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Clear Screen process has been triggered by the user pressing PF4
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Initialize All Fields routine executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID input field (USRIDINI) is set to spaces and the User ID field length/cursor indicator (USRIDINL) is set to -1 to position the cursor on the User ID field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear User ID Input Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the screen reset operation, the User ID input field is cleared to spaces and its cursor length indicator is reset.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Clear Screen process has been triggered by the user pressing PF4
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Initialize All Fields routine executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The First Name input field (FNAMEI) is set to spaces, removing any previously displayed user first name

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear First Name Input Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the screen reset operation, the First Name input field is cleared to spaces.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Clear Screen process has been triggered by the user pressing PF4
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Initialize All Fields routine executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Last Name input field (LNAMEI) is set to spaces, removing any previously displayed user last name

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Last Name Input Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the screen reset operation, the Last Name input field is cleared to spaces.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Clear Screen process has been triggered by the user pressing PF4
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Initialize All Fields routine executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User Type input field (USRTYPEI) is set to spaces, removing any previously displayed user type value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear User Type Input Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the screen reset operation, the User Type input field is cleared to spaces.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Clear Screen process has been triggered by the user pressing PF4, and there may be an existing message (error or informational) displayed on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Initialize All Fields routine executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message field (WS-MESSAGE) is set to spaces, which clears any previously displayed error or informational message (such as 'User ID NOT found' or 'Press PF5 key to delete this user') from the screen error message area (ERRMSGO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Existing Screen Messages
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of the screen reset operation, any existing informational or error messages currently displayed on the screen are cleared.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All input fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type) and the message area have been cleared to spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Send User Deletion Screen routine executes as the final step of the Clear Screen process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with the current date, current time, transaction name, and program name; the empty message (spaces) is moved to the screen error message area (ERRMSGO); and the User Deletion screen (COUSR3A from mapset COUSR03) is sent to the user with the cursor positioned on the User ID field, displaying a fully cleared and reset screen ready for new input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Empty User Deletion Screen After Clear
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all fields and messages have been cleared, the system refreshes and redisplays the User Deletion screen in its empty initial state, with updated header information including current date and time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User Delete screen and an originating program name is recorded in the session communication area (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is not blank and not empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF3 to navigate back
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the navigation destination to the originating program name stored in CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Navigation Destination When Originating Screen Is Recorded
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 to navigate back, the system checks whether an originating screen was recorded in the session. If a valid originating program name exists, it is used as the navigation destination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User Delete screen and no originating program name is recorded in the session communication area (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is blank or empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF3 to navigate back
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the navigation destination to the Administration Menu screen (COADM01C)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Navigation Destination to Admin Menu When No Originating Screen Is Recorded
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 to navigate back, if no originating program name is recorded in the session (the field is blank or empty), the system defaults the navigation destination to the Administration Menu screen (COADM01C).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The navigation destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is blank or empty at the time of screen transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to navigate to the destination screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system overrides the blank destination and sets it to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) before proceeding with navigation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Safety Fallback to Sign-On Screen When Destination Is Still Undefined
all_rules.Rule_Description: As a safety measure during the navigation process, if the destination program is still undefined (blank or empty) at the point of transfer, the system defaults to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to prevent navigation failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined the navigation destination and is ready to transfer control
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The navigation to the destination screen is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) into CDEMO-FROM-TRANID and the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) into CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM in the session communication area, and resets the program context to zero before transferring control

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Program as Originating Program Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the destination screen, the system records the current transaction ID and program name in the session communication area so the destination screen knows which program initiated the navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The navigation destination has been determined (either the originating screen or the Admin Menu COADM01C) and the current program details have been recorded in the session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the navigation transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers control to the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) and passes the full session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) to the destination screen, ending execution of the current program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Destination Screen with Session Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system transfers full control to the determined destination screen, passing along the entire session communication area so that the destination screen has access to all session context and navigation history.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User Delete screen and has interacted with the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF12 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the target destination program to the Admin Menu screen (COADM01C)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Admin Menu as Navigation Destination on PF12
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF12, the system sets the navigation destination to the Admin Menu screen (COADM01C) before initiating the navigation process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination has been set to the Admin Menu screen (COADM01C) after PF12 was pressed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to the Admin Menu
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction ID into the originating transaction field, records the current program name into the originating program field, and resets the program context to zero in the communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Program as Originating Screen Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before navigating away to the Admin Menu, the system records the current program name and transaction ID as the originating screen, so the navigation history is preserved in the communication area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination is confirmed as Admin Menu (COADM01C), and the current program has been recorded as the originating screen in the communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the navigation transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the Admin Menu screen (COADM01C) with the full communication area passed along to maintain session state, and the User Delete screen is exited

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate to Admin Menu Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After setting the destination and recording the originating program, the system transfers control to the Admin Menu screen (COADM01C), passing the full communication area to maintain session context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Deletion screen is active and waiting for user input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key other than Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5, or PF12
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error indicator flag to 'Y' (error condition active), signaling that an invalid key was pressed and that an error response must be triggered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Unsupported Key Press on User Deletion Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses any key that is not one of the supported function keys (Enter, PF3, PF4, PF5, PF12) on the User Deletion screen, the system must identify it as an invalid action and set an error indicator to trigger the appropriate error response.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error indicator has been set to active due to an unsupported key press on the User Deletion screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the error response for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system loads the standard application-defined invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) into the screen message field (WS-MESSAGE) to be displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Load Invalid Key Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unsupported key is detected on the User Deletion screen, the system must load the standard invalid key error message into the screen message area to inform the user that their key press was not recognized.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to redisplay the User Deletion screen following an invalid key press
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population routine is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the screen header with: Application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01), Application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02), the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID), the current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME), the current date formatted as MM-DD-YY (derived from system current date), and the current time formatted as HH-MM-SS (derived from system current time)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Header Before Redisplay
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before redisplaying the User Deletion screen after an invalid key press, the system must refresh the screen header with current contextual information including application titles, program name, transaction ID, current date, and current time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error indicator is active, the invalid key error message has been loaded into the message field, and the screen header has been populated with current date, time, transaction ID, and program name
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the User Deletion screen back to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the User Deletion screen (COUSR3A from mapset COUSR03) with the invalid key error message visible in the error message area (ERRMSGO), the refreshed header information, and the cursor positioned for user input, then waits for the next user key press

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay User Deletion Screen with Invalid Key Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: After detecting an invalid key press and loading the error message, the system must redisplay the User Deletion screen showing the invalid key error message to the user, preserving the current screen state and awaiting the next valid user input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Delete screen is about to be displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population process is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time and stores it in the working date-time data area (WS-CURDATE-DATA) for use in subsequent header formatting steps

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the screen header, the system retrieves the current system date and time to ensure the header always reflects accurate and up-to-date information at the moment of display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress and the current system date and time have been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Application titles are being set for the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system places the standard application Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) into the screen header Title 1 output field (TITLE01O) and the standard application Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) into the screen header Title 2 output field (TITLE02O)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Application Titles on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen header must display two standard application title lines sourced from the central application constants area (CCDA), ensuring consistent branding across all screens.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress and application titles have been set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Program identification information is being placed on the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system places the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) into the Transaction Name output field (TRNNAMEO) and the current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME) into the Program Name output field (PGMNAMEO) on the screen header

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Program Name and Transaction ID on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen header must display the current program name and transaction ID to provide users with context about which program and transaction they are currently operating in.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress, program information has been set, and the raw system date is available in WS-CURDATE-DATA
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current date is being formatted for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts the month portion from the system date into WS-CURDATE-MM, the day portion into WS-CURDATE-DD, and the last two digits of the year (characters 3 and 4 of the year field) into WS-CURDATE-YY, composing the final formatted date value WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY in MM-DD-YY format

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Current Date as MM-DD-YY for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current date must be formatted in MM-DD-YY format before being displayed on the screen header, ensuring a consistent and user-friendly date presentation across all screens.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress, the date has been formatted, and the raw system time is available in WS-CURDATE-DATA
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current time is being formatted for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system extracts the hours portion from the system time into WS-CURTIME-HH, the minutes portion into WS-CURTIME-MM, and the seconds portion into WS-CURTIME-SS, composing the final formatted time value WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS in HH:MM:SS format

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Current Time as HH-MM-SS for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current time must be formatted in HH:MM:SS format before being displayed on the screen header, ensuring a consistent and user-friendly time presentation across all screens.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is in progress and both the formatted date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) and formatted time (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) have been computed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All header details are being placed onto the screen output area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system moves the formatted date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) into the Current Date output field (CURDATEO) on the screen and moves the formatted time (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) into the Current Time output field (CURTIMEO) on the screen, completing the header population

all_rules.Rule_Name: Place All Formatted Header Details onto Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once all header components are prepared, the formatted date and time values must be placed into the screen output area so they are visible to the user on every screen display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Any event requires the User Delete screen to be displayed, including initial display, error redisplay after failed lookup, error redisplay after failed deletion, successful lookup display, successful deletion confirmation display, or screen clear display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Send User Delete Screen process is triggered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Screen Header Population on Every Screen Display

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the Delete User screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Missing Active Session on Delete User Screen Access
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user attempts to access the Delete User screen, the system must verify that an active session exists (communication area is present). If no active session is found, the user must be redirected away from the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the session is missing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Sign-On Screen as Redirect Destination for Unauthenticated Access
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no active session is detected, the system must designate the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) as the target destination before performing the redirect.

Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control away from the Delete User screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Program and Transaction Details Before Redirect

Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the redirect

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redirect Unauthenticated User to Sign-On Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After recording navigation context, the system must transfer control to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C), passing the communication area so that session state is maintained for the sign-on process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An administrator has entered a non-blank User ID on the User Delete screen and pressed the ENTER key

all_rules.Rule_Name: Search User Security File by User ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an administrator initiates a user lookup, the system searches the User Security File (USRSEC) using the entered User ID as the search key to retrieve the user record for review and potential deletion.

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Record Found - Retrieve User Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User ID is found in the USRSEC User Security File, the system retrieves and displays the user's personal and role details on the screen for administrator review before deletion.

Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user record is confirmed as found and user details are populated on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Deletion Confirmation Prompt After Successful User Lookup

Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the User Delete screen to the administrator
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen displays the user's First Name, Last Name, and User Type alongside the User ID, along with the confirmation prompt message 'Press PF5 key to delete this user...', allowing the administrator to review all details before proceeding

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User Details for Administrator Review Before Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system presents the retrieved user's full profile on the delete screen so the administrator can verify the correct user record before confirming deletion.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Allow Administrator to Retry with a Different User ID After Not Found Error

Acceptance_Criteria.When: The search of the USRSEC User Security File fails due to an unexpected condition other than 'record not found'

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Security File Lookup Failure - Display System Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the USRSEC User Security File lookup cannot be completed due to an unexpected system condition, the system notifies the administrator that the lookup operation failed.

Acceptance_Criteria.When: The deletion is completed successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All screen input fields are cleared: User ID is set to spaces, First Name is set to spaces, Last Name is set to spaces, User Type is set to spaces, and the message area is cleared to spaces

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Screen Fields After Successful User Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful deletion of a user record, all input fields on the User Delete screen must be cleared to reset the screen to a clean state, ready for the next operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the confirmation message for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system builds the success message by concatenating 'User ', the deleted User ID (trimmed of trailing spaces), and ' has been deleted ...' into a single message string, displays this message in green color on the User Delete screen, and refreshes the screen with the cleared fields and the green success message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build and Display Green Success Message After User Deletion
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully deleting a user and clearing the screen fields, the system constructs a personalized confirmation message incorporating the deleted User ID and displays it in green color to visually confirm the successful deletion to the operator.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User Not Found Error When Deletion Target Does Not Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the user record targeted for deletion cannot be located in the User Security File at the time of the delete operation, the system must notify the operator with a specific not-found error message and return the screen for correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', displays the error message 'Unable to Update User...' on the screen, positions the cursor on the First Name field, and redisplays the User Delete screen for the operator to take corrective action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Deletion Failure Error When User Record Cannot Be Deleted
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the deletion of a user record from the User Security File fails for any reason other than the record not being found (e.g., file unavailable, access conflict), the system must notify the operator with a generic deletion failure error message and return the screen.

description:
COUSR03C is a CICS online program within the CardDemo application that provides the functionality to delete a user record from the USRSEC security file. The program presents a user deletion screen, allows an operator to look up a user by User ID, displays the user's details for confirmation, and upon pressing PF5, permanently removes the user record from the system. This is a Main/Driver program that manages its own screen interactions and navigation flow.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: VSAM/CICS File (USRSEC) - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Initialize Delete User Screen - When the user deletion screen is first accessed, initialize the screen display and pre-populate the User ID field if a user was already selected from a previous screen, then display the user deletion screen 2: Validate User ID Entry - When the user presses Enter or initiates a delete, validate that the User ID field is not empty; if empty, display an error message 'User ID can NOT be empty...' and prompt the user to enter a valid User ID 3: Look Up User Details - Search for the entered User ID in the user security file; if found, retrieve and display the user's first name, last name, and user type on the screen along with a prompt message 'Press PF5 key to delete this user...' 4: Display User Not Found Error - If the entered User ID does not exist in the user security file, display an error message 'User ID NOT found...' and allow the user to enter a different User ID 5: Display User Details for Confirmation - After successfully finding the user, display the user's information (User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type) on the screen so the administrator can confirm before deletion 6: Delete User Record - When the user presses PF5, validate the User ID is not empty, look up the user in the security file, and permanently delete the user record from the user security file 7: Confirm Successful User Deletion - After successfully deleting the user, clear all screen fields, display a green success message 'User [UserID] has been deleted...' to confirm the deletion was completed 8: Clear Screen Fields - When the user presses PF4, clear all input fields on the screen (User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type) and reset the screen to its initial empty state 9: Navigate to Previous Screen - When the user presses PF3, return to the screen that originally called this program (or default to the Admin Menu screen COADM01C if no originating program is recorded) 10: Navigate to Admin Menu - When the user presses PF12, navigate directly to the Admin Menu screen (COADM01C) 11: Handle Invalid Key Press - When the user presses any key other than the supported function keys, display an error message indicating an invalid key was pressed and redisplay the current screen 12: Populate Screen Header Information - On every screen display, populate the screen header with the application title, program name, transaction ID, current date, and current time 13: Redirect Unauthenticated Session - If the program is accessed without an active session (no communication area), redirect the user to the sign-on screen (COSGN00C)
